prime.problem: Nine lectures in a row can feel like nine separate topics. Without the line that connects them, you can't say why BatchNorm comes before WaveNet, or what GPT-2 reuses from micrograd, and each new lecture feels like starting over.
prime.fits: Third card of the series map. It places every course on one factory line, so each later course's Prime ("where it fits") points back to a station you've seen here.
expect: the loss falling station by station on the same dataset
what stays constant: backprop and the training loop
prime.goal: Draw the factory line from memory with course numbers, and say in one line what each station adds to the one before.

attend: Where on the line does the series switch from single numbers to tensors, and what does it keep from the scalar part?
Which stations change the model, and which change how it's trained or checked?
Why can the names-dataset losses from z2h-3 to z2h-7 be compared (roughly), but not with z2h-8's?
What is left for z2h-10 to add, if the Transformer already exists at z2h-8?

must: Every station keeps the same loop (forward → loss → backward → update) → only the model or its conditioning changes → each loss drop can be traced to one named change

More context per prediction → better next-character guesses → 2.454 (1 char, counts) → 2.1701 (3 chars, MLP) → 1.9937 (8 chars, WaveNet) → the Transformer's attention lets every position use all earlier ones
Deeper nets train badly at init → Kaiming init and BatchNorm (z2h-5) keep activations healthy → the deeper WaveNet and Transformer become trainable
The micrograd graph and loss.backward() compute the same thing → z2h-6 proves it on tensors → at z2h-10 backprop is taken for granted and the work is speed and scale
elevated: The tokenizer is its own stage with its own training → it decides what a "token" is before the GPT sees anything → which is why it can be studied right after z2h-8's first cards
reference: which Karpathy repo holds each lecture's code
the val losses to four decimals

compress.prompt: Course-level compress: draw the factory line from memory, 12 stations with their z2h numbers, as a snake of three rows. Under each arrow, write in three words or fewer what the next station adds.
checklist: bigram counts (3) → MLP language model (4) → BatchNorm + init (5) → backprop by hand (6)
at least three of the loss or context numbers in the right order

retrieve.q: Explain why the series starts with an engine for single numbers instead of going straight to tensors, even though nobody trains real nets on scalars.
answer: each scalar op has a derivative you can check by hand
backprop is the same algorithm on tensors, just batched
so every later loss.backward() is something you've already built and understood

retrieve.q: Trace one training step's journey along the line from the MLP language model (z2h-4) to WaveNet (z2h-7): what gets added to the model, and what stays the same?
answer: z2h-4: embeddings, a tanh hidden layer, 3 characters of context
z2h-5: Kaiming init and a BatchNorm layer, plus diagnostics
z2h-6: the same net, backprop by hand (the model doesn't change)
z2h-7: 8 characters of context fused in a tree, torch.nn-style layers
the same: cross-entropy loss, minibatch SGD, the names dataset

retrieve.q: Someone wants to skip z2h-5 and z2h-6 to reach GPT sooner. What would they lose, and which of the two is the safer skip?
answer: z2h-5: why deep nets fail at init and how normalisation fixes it, which the Transformer's LayerNorm and init rely on
z2h-6: fluency with tensor gradients, which you rarely need to write once autograd exists
z2h-6 is the safer skip (the series marks it recommended, not required, for z2h-7)

compare.q: micrograd's big-ideas card compresses one lecture, and this card compresses the series. Which of micrograd's six ideas are still true unchanged at GPT-2, and which ones become engineering problems?
answer: unchanged: the net is one expression, backprop is the chain rule, reused values accumulate gradients, and the loop
engineering at scale: speed (one node per tensor op, fused kernels), memory and batch size
the math is identical; the cost is what changes

compare.q: This line ends at a pretrained GPT-2. The z2h-8 card says how a decoder-only GPT becomes ChatGPT. Which stations would you have to add after z2h-10 to reach a chat model, and which existing station changes least?
answer: new stations: supervised finetuning on conversations, then preference or reinforcement learning
the model and the training loop barely change; the data and the objective do
the tokenizer station changes least (it only gains special tokens for the chat format)

predict.q: Imagine a 13th station after GPT-2 that just makes the model 10× bigger with the same data and code. Commit first: which part of the line would you have to revisit, and which would you not touch?
predict.answer: You'd revisit the speed and scale parts of z2h-10 (memory, batch size, multi-GPU, the learning-rate recipe) and possibly init, because deeper and wider nets are exactly what z2h-5's lessons are about. You wouldn't touch backprop (z2h-2, z2h-6), the loss, or the tokenizer. The architecture stays a Transformer (z2h-8), just with more layers and heads. That's why the line is worth learning in order: scaling reuses it rather than replacing it.
